nodes.label: Ophanim E2EE Messaging Platform
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Mission is to make E2EE communication reachable by anyone with a browser; differentiator is browser-native PGP with no installs, accounts, or tracking, targeting journalists, activists, and security researchers.

nodes.label: Zero-Knowledge Relay Architecture
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: The server is deliberately a dumb pipe that relays PGP ciphertext and never stores or decrypts messages, so a full server compromise yields no plaintext; the trade-off is that metadata (IP, timing, room codes) remains out of scope.

nodes.label: OphanimCrypto API
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: A thin wrapper over OpenPGP.js v5 exposing generateKeyPair, encryptMessage, decryptMessage, signMessage, verifySignature, getFingerprint, and generateRoomCode so every page shares one crypto surface instead of calling OpenPGP directly.

nodes.label: OpenPGP.js v5
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: 552KB client-side library chosen to keep all cryptography in the browser; its weight is accepted as the cost of zero-knowledge operation.

nodes.label: ECC Curve25519 Key Generation
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Curve25519 chosen over RSA for fast in-browser keygen (~200-500ms) and brute-force resistance; private keys are protected at rest with AES-256 derived from a user passphrase, and signing uses EdDSA/Ed25519.

nodes.label: Kill Switch
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: A broadcast socket event that makes every client in a room wipe chat history instantly, added specifically to mitigate forced disclosure / coercion scenarios.

nodes.label: Express + Socket.IO Relay Server
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Holds only in-memory room state and serves static files; persistence is deliberately omitted so there is nothing to seize or subpoena.

nodes.label: Socket.IO Event Protocol (join-room, message, kill-switch, typing)
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Clients send an array of per-recipient ciphertexts rather than one blob, because PGP encryption is per public key and the server must never be able to combine or read them.

nodes.label: Ophanim Threat Model
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Explicitly protects against server compromise, MITM on content, message persistence, forced disclosure, and key brute force; only partially addresses key-exchange integrity (manual fingerprint verification) and browser compromise (localStorage risk); declares metadata analysis, client-side malware, and physical device access out of scope.

nodes.label: Ophanim Dark Cyberpunk Design System
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Near-black #07070d ground with purple #a855f7 / cyan #06b6d4 / pink #ec4899 accents, Inter for body and JetBrains Mono for keys and ciphertext, glassmorphism cards and 16px radii — a deliberately premium cyberpunk register meant to make a security tool feel trustworthy rather than utilitarian.

nodes.label: Crypto Test Suite (test.html)
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: A minimal developer page, deliberately without glassmorphism, that exercises key generation, encryption, decryption, signing, verification, wrong-passphrase rejection, and room-code generation with timings.

nodes.label: Ophanim Future Roadmap
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Group key rotation and file/image encryption are P1; Tor/I2P integration and multi-device key sync are deferred to P3 research because of high complexity.

nodes.label: Google Stitch Layout Prompts
nodes.author: Joshua
nodes.rationale: Per-page natural-language design briefs kept in the PRD so UI generation stays anchored to the documented design tokens rather than drifting per page.
